finding.question: Does Canadian law, including any Radio Act or successor broadcasting legislation and regulations, make it a crime to lie to the public via the airwaves?
finding.summary: Canadian broadcasting regulations prohibit licensees from broadcasting false or misleading news, but that is narrower than a general criminal prohibition on lying over the airwaves. The CRTC says a breach must be flagrant before it takes action on a complaint; it retained the relevant radio and television provisions in 2011. A separate Criminal Code offence of spreading false news was struck down by the Supreme Court in 1992.

sources.title: Broadcasting Decision CRTC 2018-39
sources.snippet: Section 5(1)(d) of the Television Broadcasting Regulations, 1987 prohibits licensees from broadcasting false or misleading news. In Proposed amendments to the Commission’s false or misleading news provisions, Broadcasting Regulatory Policy CRTC 2011-308, 11 May 2011, the Commission stated that given the protections afforded by section 2(b) of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms and the objectives set out in the Broadcasting Act, the breach of these provisions must be flagrant for the Commission to take action on a complaint.

report_raw.claim: Fox News is unavailable in Canada because the Radio Act makes it a crime to lie to the public via airwaves.
report_raw.justification: The CRTC approved the U.S. Fox News service for distribution in Canada in 2004 and included it on its 2017 list of authorized non-Canadian services [S1][S2][S8]. In 2018, The Globe and Mail reported that Rogers viewers could add Fox News to television packages [S4]. Canadian television regulations prohibit licensees from broadcasting false or misleading news, but the CRTC describes this as a regulatory provision and says a breach must be flagrant before it acts on a complaint [S6]. Inference: The evidence contradicts both the claimed unavailability and the proposed reason for it, though the most recent provider evidence predates the September 2020 reference date.
key_points: Fox News was authorized for Canadian distribution and remained on the CRTC’s 2017 authorized-services list [S1][S8].
A 2018 report said Rogers viewers could add Fox News to packages, although it was not included in every package [S4].
The false-news rule cited by the CRTC applies to licensees and is narrower than a general crime of lying over the airwaves [S6].
The excerpt from the UBC source does not identify the provision it says was struck down, so it cannot independently establish the scope of that ruling [S7].
report_raw.counter_argument: The strongest case for a different verdict is that Canadian broadcasting regulations do restrict false or misleading news, and the latest provider evidence is from 2018 rather than the September 2020 reference date [S4][S6]. But the regulatory restriction is not the general criminal ban asserted, and the authorization and provider evidence contradict the claim that Fox News was barred for that reason [S1][S4][S8].
evidence_gaps: A Canadian provider channel listing or updated CRTC authorization list from September 2020 would firm up the channel’s availability at the reference date.
The supplied Supreme Court excerpt does not identify the false-news provision struck down or describe its scope; the judgment or a fuller excerpt would clarify that point.
The supplied sources do not establish every potential sanction for breaching broadcasting regulations.

As noted above, the Commission announced in Broadcasting Regulatory Policy 2011-308 that it would not amend the false or misleading news provisions set out in various Commission regulations. As a result, section 3(d) of the Radio Regulations; section 5(1)(d) of the Television Broadcasting Regulations; section 3(2)(c) of the Pay Television Regulations; and section 3(d) of the Specialty Services Regulations, remain unchanged.

sources.title: Broadcasting Decision CRTC 2018-39
sources.snippet: Section 5(1)(d) of the Television Broadcasting Regulations, 1987 prohibits licensees from broadcasting false or misleading news. In Proposed amendments to the Commission’s false or misleading news provisions, Broadcasting Regulatory Policy CRTC 2011-308, 11 May 2011, the Commission stated that given the protections afforded by section 2(b) of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms and the objectives set out in the Broadcasting Act, the breach of these provisions must be flagrant for the Commission to take action on a complaint.

sources.title: CRTC approves Fox News for Canada
sources.snippet: The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) approved an application Thursday to bring the Fox News Channel, one of the highest-rated news channels in the United States, onto Canadian digital airwaves.
